contracts_to_satisfy.deterministic_fusion: lexical and vector rankings fused by a deterministic rule
contracts_to_satisfy.no_double_counting: the same WikiPage must not gain weight from multiple mirrors
contracts_to_satisfy.score_breakdown: when channel == FUSED, score_breakdown MUST be present
contracts_to_satisfy.index_is_derived: the vector index may only be derived from canonical WikiPage content - never a source of truth
contracts_to_satisfy.incremental_sync: new page or new revision is searchable after incremental sync
contracts_to_satisfy.index_rebuild: index can be fully rebuilt from canonical WikiPage content
contracts_to_satisfy.degradation: vector unavailable -> lexical fallback with the degradation state recorded

deliverables: deterministic fusion over lexical + vector + graph candidates
mirror de-duplication that never double-counts the same page
score_breakdown / channel / matched_stage on each RetrievalHit
index build, incremental sync and full rebuild from canonical content
index version tracking and detection of version changes
a comparison report: RRF vs simple weighted fusion vs field filtering
task-local ledger, L3 record, progress log and handoff

positive: same two-path input yields a stable, consistent fused ranking
duplicate mirrors do NOT increase the score
a newly added WikiPage becomes searchable
rebuilding the index from canonical content yields the same results
decision_evidence: MUST produce a lexical-only vs hybrid comparison report and let the EVIDENCE decide the fusion strategy
RRF must NOT be the default without that evidence - the M11 partitions are SMALL corpora where RRF is known to add little or even hurt
